Armed Conflict & Security
• Former DR Congo president Joseph Kabila is named leader of a new rebel coalition, amid ongoing M23 control of much of the east.
• Bulgaria summoned Russia’s ambassador after a cargo ship sank in a suspected Black Sea drone attack, with 11 crew missing.
• A large cyberattack overheated hundreds of French supermarket fridges, spoiling food and sparking fires, raising food security concerns.
• Iran warned Gulf states of potential attacks on regional cables and data centers, highlighting internet infrastructure vulnerabilities.
• Both Russia and Ukraine are deploying AI-powered first-person-view drones on the battlefield, accelerating automation in warfare.
Why it matters: Conflicts are increasingly converging with cyber and AI capabilities, threatening civilians, commerce and critical infrastructure beyond the front lines.

Society & Human Rights
• Hungary’s parliament scrapped several Orbán-era anti-LGBTQ measures, welcomed by activists who seek broader reforms.
• US immigration agents searched Rep. Ilhan Omar’s Washington home, which she called political targeting; federal ad spending for Trump also drew scrutiny.
• India’s opposition escalated protests over voter list revisions they say favor the ruling party, with leaders detained in Delhi.
• Jury selection begins in the hate crimes trial of the Buffalo supermarket gunman, who could face the death penalty.
• Iraqi women reporting sexual violence say they face threats and social isolation for speaking out.
Why it matters: Rights protections, fair elections and accountability remain contested across democracies, affecting public trust and vulnerable communities.

Climate & Environment
• A “super” El Niño has strengthened to unprecedented levels, with multiple indicators in record territory.
• El Niño-fueled wildfires in Indonesia razed nearly 300 homes and worsened haze, while damaged peatlands continue to burn.
• The land carbon sink rebounded in 2025 due to favorable conditions but may slump again under El Niño next year.
• Argentina temporarily closed access to Iguazu Falls after heavy rains drove river flows to six times normal rates.
• UN carbon market rules will require cookstove projects to cover risks of later forest loss, tightening integrity of credits.
Why it matters: Intensifying climate signals are translating into immediate impacts on ecosystems, health, tourism and carbon accounting integrity.

Health & Pandemic

• Pennsylvania reported a sixth measles death amid more than 1,100 cases, with the latest victim unvaccinated.

Why it matters: High-profile health events and resurgent outbreaks underscore the need for transparency and vaccination to manage risk.

Why it matters: AI-driven volatility and macro risks are reshaping markets, while earnings and restructurings reflect shifting business fundamentals.

Entertainment.text: Name: Prada America's Cup sneakerColorway: Teak/Blue, Cacao/BordeauxSKU: TBCMSRP: TBCRelease Date: October 13Where to Buy: PradaPrada revisits one of its most recognizable footwear silhouettes with a new release of the America’s Cup sneaker, introducing two colorways: “Teak/Blue” and “Cacao/Bordeaux.”Originally conceived in 1997 for the Luna Rossa sailing team, the model retains the streamlined, aerodynamic profile and technical sensibility that have defined it for nearly three decades. Staying true to the beloved original silhouette, the updated America's Cup sneaker maintains its distinctive, multi-layered construction. The upper showcases a dynamic interplay of textures, combining smooth, glossy patent leather overlays with highly breathable, technical textile mesh panels.While the aesthetic heritage and signature Linea Rossa heel branding remain completely intact, the footwear receives a significant modern upgrade underfoot with the introduction of an innovative, ultra-lightweight rubber sole. This technical enhancement ensures the shoe delivers superior modern comfort and everyday wearability without sacrificing the rugged, utilitarian charm that made the 1997 original a global streetwear staple."Teak/Blue" pairs warm brown tones with cooler blue accents, while "Cacao/Bordeaux" shifts into a richer combination of deep chocolate brown and wine-red hues. Both treatments emphasize the sneaker’s distinctive interplay of textile and leather, using changes in material and tone to accentuate the curved paneling and elongated lines of the upper rather than dramatically altering the familiar shape.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Entertainment.title: Beats Catches Pikachu and Mimikyu for Its First Charm-Loaded Pill Speaker
Entertainment.text: SummaryBeats and The Pokémon Company International have teamed up on a special-edition Pill speaker dressed in Pikachu’s electric yellow and a grayscale take on MimikyuA set of bespoke charms, interactive packaging and a color-matched lanyard round out the collectible designUnder the costume sits the standard Pill hardware, including USB-C lossless audio, up to 24 hours of playback and IP67 dust and water resistanceBeats has joined forces with The Pokémon Company International on the special-edition Pokémon x Beats Pill, a portable Bluetooth speaker built around two fan-favorite Pokémon. Pikachu and Mimikyu share the spotlight across the speaker’s grill and body, pairing a high-voltage color story with a moodier monochrome counterpart.Both Pokémon appear on the speaker grill, with the front and back of the Pill split between two visual identities. Pikachu supplies the bright, unmistakable yellow, while Mimikyu is rendered in shades of gray, setting up a contrast between bold energy and quiet mystery. The duo is a fitting match, since Mimikyu is known in the games for disguising itself under a homemade Pikachu costume.The accessories mark a first for the line. This is the debut of charms on a Beats Pill, and the special edition includes a bespoke set featuring a Poké Ball, the Beats “b” logo and lightning bolts that nod to Pikachu’s signature move set. The packaging gets its own interactive design treatment as well, giving collectors a reason to hold onto the box.On the audio side, the Pill runs a custom acoustic system tuned for deep bass and sound big enough to fill a room. Plugging in via USB-C unlocks high-resolution lossless playback, and owners of two Pills can link them wirelessly in either Amplify Mode for more volume or Stereo Mode for left and right separation.The speaker is built to travel, with up to 24 hours of battery life and an IP67 rating against dust and water that makes it safe for the gym, the beach or a backyard. A removable lanyard matched to the colorway and a soft-grip silicone back make it easy to carry, and the included USB-C cable lets the Pill double as a power bank for a compatible phone.For Beats, the project is less about novelty and more about meeting an already devoted audience where it lives. “Pokémon Trainers are some of the most passionate in the world, and we saw an opportunity to channel that energy into something fun, unexpected, and created especially for fans,” said Beats CMO Chris Thorne in the announcement. The result treats a familiar speaker as a canvas for fandom, with every design choice tied back to the two characters on its face.The special-edition Pokémon x Beats Pill launches October 15 via Apple and Target (online and select stores) in the US, via Apple and Argos (online and select stores) in the UK, and via Apple and Douyin in China.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Entertainment.title: Wrangler and ROA Reimagine Denim Workwear for FW26
Entertainment.text: SummaryWrangler and ROA reunite for their second collaboration, blending American denim heritage with Italian technical design.The FW26 capsule features denim cargos, hooded jackets and caps in two washes.Inspired by a Swedish lumberjack's training routines, the collection launches today.Wrangler and ROA are returning for a second collaboration for Fall/Winter 2026, continuing their exploration of the intersection between American denim heritage and Italian technical design. Building on their debut collection, the latest release revisits Wrangler's workwear roots through ROA's outdoor-oriented perspective, presenting a concise lineup designed around utility, durability and everyday versatility.The three-piece capsule comprises the Wrangler x ROA Denim Cargo, Denim Hooded Jacket and Denim 6 Panel Cap, each offered in two washes: Owl Dark and Owl Light. Together, the pieces establish a cohesive denim wardrobe that draws on traditional workwear while reflecting ROA's functional design sensibilities, with the contrasting washes offering different interpretations of the same utilitarian aesthetic.The collection's accompanying narrative takes inspiration from Edvin, a 26-year-old forestry teacher from Orsa, a small town in northern Sweden, as he prepares for a professional lumberjack championship. Rather than focusing on the competition itself, the story turns its attention to the discipline and routines that precede it, from training in the woods and maintaining equipment to sharpening axes, traveling and recovering between sessions.Through this perspective, the collaboration places the everyday realities of physical work and preparation at the center of its visual identity, reinforcing the relationship between purposeful clothing and the environments in which it is worn. The second Wrangler x ROA collection launches on October 13, 2026, and will be available online through ROA's official website and Wrangler.com.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Entertainment.title: Breitling Gives Aston Martin Valhalla Owners Their Own Bespoke Super Chronomat
Entertainment.text: SummaryBreitling opens a bespoke Super Chronomat program exclusively for Aston Martin Valhalla owners.Buyers can customize two Super Chronomat models with car-inspired colors and personal engravings.Options include a B19 perpetual calendar chronograph and 38mm diamond-set automatic.Breitling and Aston Martin have deepened their partnership with a highly exclusive bespoke program designed solely for owners of the Aston Martin Valhalla supercar. Reflecting the engineering and aerodynamic mastery of the limited-production, 1,079 PS hybrid Valhalla, Breitling has opened the design process of its distinctive Super Chronomat collection to these select clients. Through a dedicated configurator, owners can commission a timepiece that mirrors their individual vehicle specification and personal taste, merging the high-performance worlds of British automotive design and Swiss watchmaking.The bespoke program offers two distinct models for customization, the first being the Super Chronomat B19 44 Perpetual Calendar Chronograph. Housed in a 44mm titanium case on Breitling’s signature Rouleaux bracelet, this model boasts a complex automatic perpetual calendar chronograph movement that requires no major manual adjustments until the year 2100. It features a carbon-fiber dial, a 96-hour power reserve, and a display caseback that showcases a personalized rotor. Valhalla owners can further customize the timepiece by selecting from a range of exclusive colors for the rehaut, seconds hand, and counter hands.The second option is the Super Chronomat Automatic 38, which balances performance materials with a refined 38mm stainless-steel case and a diamond-set bezel. This three-hand automatic model also incorporates a textured carbon-fiber dial and offers customizable colors for the rehaut and hands, as well as a personalized caseback engraving. Both bespoke timepieces provide an unparalleled ownership experience, which is further enhanced by a complimentary five-year membership to the upcoming Breitling Social Club in New York, set to open in late 2027.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Entertainment.title: The 2027 Jeep Wrangler Switchback Debuts With Custom Look
Entertainment.text: SummaryJeep drops the 2027 Wrangler Switchback, closing out its monthly "Twelve 4 Twelve" special edition campaignThe factory-built custom aesthetic features swapped doors and hoods in Gloss Black and Sting-Gray colorwaysOrders open in November with prices starting at $66,695 USD for the two-door Rubicon X-based configurationJeep officially pulled the cover off the 2027 Jeep Wrangler Switchback, serving as the twelfth and final model in its yearlong special edition rollout. Closing out the brand's ambitious "Twelve 4 Twelve" campaign, which dropped one unique Wrangler iteration every month for an entire year, the Wrangler Switchback arrives with a heavy nod to custom off-road culture. The factory-produced contrasting colorway emulates a raw, aggressive look seen on owner-modified Wranglers. By leaning into an aesthetic where mismatched body panels are historically added to achieve a custom multicolored look or replace pieces damaged during off-roading, Jeep transforms a garage-repair necessity into a factory-backed statement piece.To achieve these contrasting color schemes on the factory floor, Jeep altered its standard manufacturing rhythm. The brand sequenced Gloss Black and Sting-Gray Wranglers to run sequentially down the assembly line. Line workers manually swapped the doors of consecutively sequenced vehicles during the production cycle. Factory workers later switched the hoods during the final upfitting process. This manufacturing sequence results in two distinct mismatched exterior configurations. One configuration features gray bodywork, contrasting black doors and a matching black hood. The second option flips that color scheme, producing Wranglers with black bodywork, contrasting gray doors and a gray hood.Beyond the panel swaps, the Wrangler Switchback features vibrant Gecko accents across its exterior. Bright hits of color appear on the front grille, exterior wheel rings, bold hood graphic and rear swing-gate decal. That attention to detail extends into the cabin, where the interior features premium nappa leather with contrasting Sea Salt accents. Custom Lime stitching runs throughout the interior alongside Switchback-exclusive graphics.Structurally, the Wrangler Switchback is based on the high-end Wrangler Rubicon X trim, ensuring the rugged visual aesthetic is backed by heavy-duty trail capability. Enthusiasts can order the limited special edition in classic two-door or expanded four-door configurations. Adding the Switchback package increases the sticker price of a standard Rubicon X by $2,870 USD. The two-door model is priced at $66,695 USD, while the four-door model brings the total to $69,995 USD. Orders officially open in November.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Entertainment.text: SummaryKojima Productions and CASETiFY celebrate their 10th and 15th anniversaries with a collaboration.The collection features Yoji Shinkawa-designed phone cases, Death Stranding accessories and collectible cards.Launching globally on October 15, the range includes sculptural cases, character-inspired accessories and luggage.Hideo Kojima's distinctive creative universe is making its way onto everyday tech accessories as Kojima Productions teams up with CASETiFY for a limited-edition collection celebrating two major milestones: the Japanese game studio's 10th anniversary and CASETiFY's 15th anniversary.Developed in collaboration with Kojima and longtime art director Yoji Shinkawa at Kojima Productions' Tokyo headquarters, the range translates the studio's cinematic visual identity and the dystopian world of Death Stranding* *into a series of functional accessories. Other highlights include the Yoji Shinkawa Art Edition – From Sapiens to Ludens (Gold Camera Ring) Case and Ludens Emblem – Carbon Fiber Case, alongside designs referencing Death Stranding 2, the studio's anniversary, its recognizable logos and damage sensor tape motifs.The collaboration also introduces an assortment of accessories inspired by characters and objects from the Death Stranding *universe. Standouts include a Qpid Wristlet modeled after the necklace worn by protagonist Sam Porter Bridges, plush keychains depicting Dollman and the Ludens Duck, and metallic grip stands featuring the Ludens Golden Disk and Kojima Productions emblems. The release also incorporates a collectible element, with purchases accompanied by a blind-packed card featuring official studio artwork, randomly selected from several designs. Buyers of the 3D Crafted Aluminum Case will additionally receive two exclusive card designs unavailable through the wider collection.The Kojima Productions x CASETiFY collection launches globally on October 15, 2026, through CASETiFY's official website, Co-Lab app and participating CASETiFY STUDiO locations.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Art & Culture.title: James Fuentes Gallery Revisits Teruko Yokoi’s Transpacific Abstraction
Art & Culture.text: SummaryTeruko Yokoi’s A Pacific Line marks her first Los Angeles solo show in over four decades.The exhibition traces her evolution from figuration to abstraction.Works span 1954–2005, bridging Japanese aesthetics and postwar Western modernism.Teruko Yokoi’s decades-spanning practice returns to Los Angeles with A Pacific Line, a new exhibition at James Fuentes Gallery tracing the Japanese-Swiss painter’s singular path through postwar abstraction. Marking her first solo presentation in the city in more than four decades, the show carries particular resonance on the West Coast: Yokoi first arrived in the United States by ship in 1954, shortly after the end of the U.S. occupation of Japan, before enrolling at the California School of Fine Arts in San Francisco. That self-directed move became the starting point for a career shaped by continual relocation across Japan, the United States, France and Switzerland, while resisting easy placement within any single school or movement. Bringing together works made between 1954 and 2005, A Pacific Line presents Yokoi’s practice as an ongoing conversation between traditional Japanese aesthetics and postwar Western modernism.Yokoi’s early years in the U.S. marked a decisive shift from figuration toward the highly personal abstraction that would come to define her work. "Pose" from 1954 still retains the contours of a seated human figure, but its body already begins to dissolve into blocks of orange, gray and brown, anticipating her increasingly rhythmic treatment of form and color.After moving to New York in 1955, she studied with Hans Hofmann, attended the Art Students League and moved within circles that included Joan Mitchell, Kenzo Okada and Mark Rothko, while living for a period at the Chelsea Hotel with painter Sam Francis. Yet her work remained distinct from the dominant language of Abstract Expressionism. Paintings such as 1960’s "Shizen–Natur," with its deep green field, saturated blue forms and streaks of red and white, reveal a vocabulary grounded as much in Japanese calligraphy, haiku and observations of nature as in gestural abstraction. Yokoi herself described her paintings as “poems written in colors,” a sentiment rooted in childhood walks through the Kiso River landscape and early lessons in calligraphy and poetry from her father.The exhibition also follows Yokoi’s material evolution after settling permanently in Bern in 1962, where she maintained an exceptionally consistent studio practice until her death in 2020. Works such as "Herbstwald" (1965) and "Lauschen II (Nocturne)" (1969) use elongated vertical formats and concentrated fields of red, black and blue to turn landscape into something atmospheric and nearly musical, while later works increasingly explore paper and egg tempera.By the mid-1970s, Yokoi had embraced the demanding medium, eventually incorporating hand-mixed pigments, pearlescent minerals and metallic elements that shift according to light and viewing position. The 1993 diptych "Ohne Titel", for instance, expands this approach across luminous fields of yellow, blue, green and silver, while preserving the calligraphic lines and natural rhythms that connect her earliest and latest paintings. Organized in collaboration with Emerald Room | Emerald Editions and Kent Fine Art, Teruko Yokoi: A Pacific Line is on view at James Fuentes Gallery, 5015 Melrose Avenue in Los Angeles, through November 7, 2026.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Economy & Markets.title: Apple Captures Record 22% Q3 Smartphone Market Share
Economy & Markets.text: SummaryApple captured a record 22% of the global smartphone market in the third quarter of 2026Worldwide smartphone shipments plummeted 20% year-over-year to hit a 14-year lowAn ongoing memory crisis and rising device prices forced brands to prioritize profit over sheer volumeApple just carved out its largest third-quarter slice of the global smartphone market in history, defying a brutal industry-wide slump. According to a newly released report from Counterpoint Research, worldwide smartphone shipments plummeted 20% year-over-year during the third quarter of 2026. The severe double-digit drop pushed global shipments down to their absolute lowest third-quarter level in 14 years. While the report attributed the market decline to memory constraints and rising prices, it notably did not specify what that 20% decline translated to in absolute shipment numbers.Despite the broader market slump, Apple managed to elevate its global smartphone shipment share past the 20% threshold for the very first time in any third quarter. The tech heavyweight ultimately shipped 22% of all smartphones during Q3 2026, marking a significant jump from the 18% share it held in Q3 2025. This record-setting share came even as the brand navigated its own volume declines, largely driven by the absence of a base iPhone 18 model. Without that entry-level flagship, Apple experienced a smaller launch-month channel fill compared to what the full iPhone 17 lineup achieved a year earlier. To offset that higher shipment decline, the company leaned heavily on sustained market momentum from the older iPhone 17 series. Top-tier iPhone 18 Pro models logged a stronger launch than their direct predecessors, generating particularly heavy traction across China and India.Apple's historic surge rapidly closed the gap on Samsung, though the South Korean brand managed to maintain its first-place position in the global smartphone market with a 23% share. Other top five vendors took a noticeable hit during the quarter. Xiaomi secured third place with a 10% market share, followed closely by OPPO capturing a 9% shipment share. vivo rounded out the top five leaderboard by claiming an 8% share of shipments. Crucially, Xiaomi, OPPO and vivo all watched their shipment shares decline compared to their standing in Q3 2025.Faced with crippling component constraints and rising costs, OEMs increasingly shifted their strategies to prioritize profitability over sheer shipment volumes. Apple itself joined this industry-wide shift toward price hikes, though the immediate impact on its numbers was limited to the final weeks of the quarter. With the smartphone industry enduring its second consecutive quarter taking the full brunt of a massive memory crisis, the landscape fundamentally shifted to squeeze out budget-conscious buyers. Price-sensitive consumer segments face ongoing pressure from higher device prices and limited component availability, delaying any meaningful market recovery until global supply conditions improve.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Artificial Intelligence.title: Meet the Anthropic Engineer Keeping Its AI Agent Trustworthy
Artificial Intelligence.text: If you’ve ever wondered how Claude and similar AI agents can answer complex questions in seconds and where they get the information, you’re not alone.Gurmeet Saran works to find that answer every day as an engineer at Anthropic in San Francisco, the AI research company behind Claude. The IEEE senior member is developing an infrastructure to understand the mechanics behind the chatbot’s behavior and to ensure its underlying architecture produces reliable outputs.Gurmeet SaranEmployer Anthropic in San FranciscoTitle Member of technical staffMember grade IEEE senior memberAlma maters University of Kalyani, in India; Birla Institute of Technology and Science, in Pilani, India “My job is to make sure the data is accurate, structured, and trustworthy, and that private data stays private,” he says. “As I learned earlier in my career, privacy can’t be a layer you bolt on—it has to be part of the architecture from the start.” If you can’t trust the logic, he adds, you can’t make reliable claims about the behavior, and that has real safety implications.Safety is a priority for Anthropic, he says. According to Claude’s mission statement, the company wants the AI agent to be “genuinely helpful to the people it works with or on behalf of, as well as to society, while avoiding actions that are unsafe, unethical, or deceptive.” Crucial to the mission is ensuring that researchers can observe and understand how AI models behave, a challenge that is especially acute for large language models, Saran says.“We have decent tools to monitor databases and web services,” he says, “but for LLMs, we’re still figuring it out.”Solving data quality problems at Yahoo, Intuit, and MetaSaran’s interest in computing systems dates back to his childhood in Kolkata, where he logged as much time as he could in the school computer lab.“I remember the first time I used one of the computers,” he says. “What struck me was that you could write instructions, and the machine would follow them exactly. No ambiguity.“That felt magical to me.”After graduating from high school in 1999, he stayed in India to pursue advanced degrees. He earned a bachelor’s degree in electronics and telecommunication engineering in 2004 at the University of Kalyani. In 2010, he earned a master’s degree in software engineering from the Birla Institute of Technology and Science in Pilani.While a graduate student, he began his career in 2007 at Yahoo as a technical lead of the data team in Bengaluru, India. While there, he encountered the project that shaped his career trajectory: working on web analytics and business intelligence reporting solutions.“We kept running into a frustrating problem,” he recalls. “Different teams would calculate the same website metric—something like daily active site users—using slightly different logic, and end up with conflicting answers. It sounds like a small issue, but when leadership is making decisions about resource allocation and product development using that data, not knowing which number is correct becomes a problem.”The team built a central data repository with defined metrics, essentially serving as a single source of truth. Saran created a model that defined what “daily active site users” means, breaking down which events counted, how to handle edge cases (or when standard code fails), and more.With the new model, data teams across the company could rely on a standard method to determine the number of daily active users for the projects and sites they were responsible for and obtain comparable results using the same logic.From there, Saran and his team built Yahoo! Digits, an internal web analytics tool used for all the company’s products.Saran left Yahoo in 2010 to join Intuit as a staff engineer in Mountain View, Calif. He helped build the analytics infrastructure that unified data across the company’s products, including TurboTax and QuickBooks accounting software. During his tenure, Intuit developed a feature that detected fraudulent tax filings in real time. It required Saran and other engineers to build a system to protect taxpayer data while adhering to strict U.S. Internal Revenue Service policies.“IEEE operates in a lot of countries where engineers don’t have easy pathways into the global professional community. That kind of connection matters as AI development spreads beyond a handful of organizations.”“This taught me that privacy and governance can’t be layers you bolt onto software after the fact,” he says. “They have to be part of the architecture from the start.”Saran joined Meta (known as Facebook at the time) in 2016 as a lead software engineer in Menlo Park, Calif. The company was facing controversy over its video metrics: Meta publicly acknowledged an error that caused it to overstate the number of views for posted videos.“This wasn’t a coding bug; it was an architectural problem,” Saran says. He built a system that worked similarly to what he had developed at Intuit, whereby one single truth was defined to govern all video view metrics across the site.That system, Metric360, eventually became part of the site’s architecture. By the time he left Meta in 2021, he says, Metric360 was being used across the company to calculate video metrics.He left the company to become a principal software engineer at Wealthfront, a financial services company in Palo Alto, Calif. He helped build the company’s data infrastructure.Building trustworthy AI systems at AnthropicSaran joined Anthropic in 2025 as a member of the technical staff.To describe the implications of his work, he uses a medical analogy: “Imagine a doctor is monitoring a patient’s vital signs and making treatment decisions based on those numbers. What if one or a few of the medical devices used were slightly miscalibrated? Even if most readings are fine, it’s a serious problem because the difficult decisions happen in the margins.“It’s the same with AI systems. My job is essentially to make sure the instruments are giving accurate readings—that the data means what it says it means.”His job comes with high stakes and complex problems to solve.“AI agents are especially tricky to observe,” he says. “When a system is taking sequences of actions [generating conversational responses with different users], you need a way to capture what it did, what information it was working from, and whether outcomes matched what the end user expected. And you have to do all of that without exposing anyone’s private information—the systems are designed to recognize sensitive data and keep it protected as it flows through. It’s a much more demanding observability problem than anything I’ve worked on before.”Solving for system reliability while AI is still in its early days of adoption is both Saran’s passion and the problem that keeps him up at night, he says.“I think making AI systems genuinely auditable and transparent is one of the more important engineering problems of the next decade,” he says, “and it doesn’t get talked about as much as model capabilities do.”IEEE can play a role in shaping AI developmentSaran joined IEEE in March 2025.“After more than 20 years of building data infrastructure across organizations like Yahoo, Intuit, Meta, and Wealthfront,” he says, “I wanted to contribute back to the technical community through peer review, publishing, and engaging with the broader engineering research ecosystem.”He says he believes IEEE can play an essential role in shaping the future of AI through its standards work.“We have standards for everything, from building codes to software testing,” he says. “AI infrastructure needs something similar, and IEEE has the credibility and the reach to do that.”Another problem that IEEE can solve for, he says, is access: “IEEE operates in a lot of countries where engineers don’t have easy pathways into the global professional community. That kind of connection matters, especially as AI development spreads beyond a handful of organizations in a few cities.”
